main_text.p: tamenta[?] tanquam externa media fuerit pro sua voluntate ac placito operatus: sicut per cibum ac potum externa media, homin svitam sustentat.

Ezechias 4. lib. Reg cap. 20. gravi morbo conflictatus, convertit faciem suam ad parietem & oravit Dominum: tunc dixit Dominus, audivi orationem tuam, & vidi lachrymam tuam: & ecce sanavi te, die tertio ascendes templu Domini. Deinde dixit Esaias, asse te massam ficorum. Quam cum attulissent, & posuissent super hulcus ejus, curatus est.
Hunc ordinem omnes ægroti servent, primum orent Dominum: deinde medicamenta adhibeant.
Duæ: Pathologice, Die erforschung der Krankheit; Et Therapeutice, Die Artzneyung der Kranckheit.
Est prima pars Medicinæ de morbis investigandis. Morbus est affectus corporis præter naturam, à quo vitiatur actio.

Morbi duo præcipua vulgò dicuntur signa: urina & pulsus. Sed Dominus Doctor Scribonius acriter invehitur in eos, qui ex qualibet urina de quolibet morbo judicare volunt, & ostendit multis rationibus, inutilem & vanam esse illorum doctrinam, qui contendunt, omnes morbos & affectiones interiores humani corporis ex aspectu urinarum observari & videri posse, in libello de idea Medicinæ, Lemgoviæ excuso.
Pulsus est motus cordis & arteriarum. Pulsum explorant medici missa manu in carpum.
Duplex: Aut enim est ex intemperie, aut ex mala conformatione: Cuius species est continui solutio. Intem-peries quadruplex est: calida, frigida, humida, sicca,

page.notes: Reading of the first word of the page is doubtful because the left edge is damaged; the initial letter is cut off. The word "ejus" is printed "cjus" and is read as ejus. "hulcus" is kept as printed. The German black-letter words are transcribed as I read them; "Krankheit" and "Kranckheit" are the printed forms as far as legible. The final word "sicca" is printed with a letter that looks like f; read as sicca.
